en: Pediatrician Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to keep premature babies warm in rural areas lacking electricity.
The carabao, the national animal, wallows in mud to lower its body temperature and protect its skin from insect bites.
The Ifugao people engineered the Banaue Rice Terraces with stone walls that scientifically prevent soil erosion and dangerous landslides during heavy rains.
PHIVOLCS scientists used seismic monitoring and lahar warning systems to safely evacuate thousands of residents before the 1991 Mount Pinatubo eruption.
The Department of Health runs the National Immunization Program to give free vaccines that protect Filipino children from deadly diseases.
Filipinos preserve fish by making tuyo, using solar energy to remove moisture and stop bacteria from spoiling the food safely.
The government recognizes Filipino Sign Language as the national sign language to ensure deaf citizens safely understand medical and emergency instructions.
National Scientist Alfredo Santos extracted natural chemicals from oregano plants to create safe, effective mosquito repellents that prevent dengue fever.
Local Government Units enforce solid waste laws to clear clogged drainage systems, practically preventing dangerous urban flooding during typhoons.
The national Anti-Bullying Act requires schools to provide counseling and intervention to protect students from the mental health harms of bullying.
The sampaguita, our national flower, contains natural compounds that traditional herbalists use to safely reduce fevers and treat minor skin infections.
Traditional nipa huts use elevated bamboo floors and thatched roofs to maximize natural air circulation and keep interiors cool during hot summers.
